Code AI availability as mixed across the pre-AI/adopter/nonadopter panel and primary as not_stated because no formally designated primary outcome is stated. corrections.source_says: Populate the required diversity methods: cohort-level convex-hull volume, with surface area mentioned as a robustness variant; BLIP-2 captions embedded with a semantic-similarity-fine-tuned BERT model (Sentence-BERT reference 43; exact checkpoint not stated), reduced from 384 dimensions to five with UMAP. Hulls contain cohort artwork idea vectors and the common 21,384-pair SemArt baseline. Uncertainty is presented as event-study difference-in-differences estimates with bootstrapped matching and 95% confidence intervals; numerical endpoints and the supplement's detailed variance procedure were not available. These are set-level novelty/breadth measures, not assessments of artistic value.
corrections.quote: Thus, we operationalize creative expansion as the expansion of the convex hull of artworks’ core ideas over time.
corrections.locator: Journal main-text XML (PMC12407059), Materials and Methods, 'Idea feature extraction' and 'Operationalizing the idea frontier'; Fig. 1 caption; Results, 'Robustness checks'; Discussion, limitations

confirmed: Independently read the complete journal main-text XML, including all sections, figure captions, acknowledgments, supplementary-material listing, and references: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12407059/fullTextXML. No local markdown/PDF was on file. Main/supplement PDF requests to Europe PMC, PMC, and the publisher were blocked or challenged; the Europe PMC supplement API timed out. The supplement and numerical PDF/figure contents remain unverified.

source.version, title, authors, and publication metadata are supported: Science Advances 11(36), eadu5800, 3 September 2025, CC BY; the source is the journal version as full-text XML, not a preprint or a PDF read. Locator: XML front matter.

design_class = observational, context_class = observational, and core = no are supported. AI use is identified from users' own publications; random sampling of artworks and bootstrap permutations are analytic procedures, not random assignment of people to AI. No randomized people experiment, including an experiment with fewer than 50 analyzed people, is reported. Locators: Introduction, paragraph 4; Materials and Methods, 'Identifying AI adopters' and 'Production equalization for AI-assisted creators'.

The main text reports 31,076 unique creators and states '27 months from August 2021 to December 2023'; these are the source's printed wording and dates, not a recomputed calendar duration. The 21,384 SemArt image-description pairs are a historical-art baseline, not participant observations. Locators: Introduction, paragraph 4; Materials and Methods, 'Operationalizing the idea frontier'.

S1-O1 and S1-O2 substantive findings match: no significant pre-Midjourney idea-space differences; Midjourney V1 in February 2022 did not immediately expand the frontier; acceleration and more frontier-defining artworks followed Stable Diffusion 1.5, identified as October 2022 in the Introduction. Fig. 1 reports effects as proportions over the starting baseline (intercept plus treatment fixed effect), with 95% confidence intervals, not standardized mean differences. Locators: Introduction, paragraph 5; Results, 'Idea frontier expansion following text-to-image releases'; Fig. 1 caption.

S1-O3 correctly reports the initial concentration followed by broader participation: more H-creative AI-assisted creators than the nonadopter baseline by the end of 2023. Locator: Results, 'Attributing expansion to the hive mind or masterminds'; Fig. 1C.

S1-O4 and the one-line finding reproduce the narrative values: average 2.1% fewer frontier-defining artifacts after productivity equalization; 2.2% gains in the unadjusted discussion; approximately 4.3% net productivity contribution; maximum 6.6% by the end of 2023. These are frontier/vertex quantities, not person counts or pooled standardized effects. Locator: Results, 'Productivity effects, human-AI effects, and dilution effects', paragraph beginning 'Figure 4 reveals'; Fig. 4 caption.

The approximately 48% reduction in sampled AI-adopter artwork production and 200 draws/permutations used for production equalization are stated. These do not imply randomized people. Locator: Materials and Methods, 'Production equalization for AI-assisted creators'.

S1-O5 numerical wording matches the article: the top 10% of AI creators initially hold nearly 35%, later approximately 23%, described by the authors as 'a decrease of 12%'; nonadopters' top 10% maintain more than 30%. The source's '12%' wording is retained without silently recalculating or relabeling it. Locator: Results, 'AI-assisted creativity as a stochastic versus persistent process', paragraph beginning 'Examining market shares'; Fig. 3A-B.

Supplement existence and listed contents are confirmed, but the contents themselves were not read: sciadv.adu5800_sm.pdf, Supplementary Text, Figs. S1 to S6, Tables S1 to S4, References. Locator: XML 'Supplementary Materials' and associated media link.

This is an original observational study, not a synthesis; synthesis counts and pooled estimates are inapplicable. No pooled study count, pooled interval, or standardizing denominator should be supplied. Locators: Introduction; Materials and Methods.
summary: The observational classification and headline numbers match the complete main-text XML, with no randomized people study identified. Ten corrections address incomplete fields, adoption timing, mixed result direction, omitted outcomes/provenance, and quotation fidelity; PDFs and the supplement could not be accessed.
